stories.headline: Update: U.S. and Iran Resume Strikes as Brief Pause Collapses; Russian Missile Lands in Poland
stories.summary:
The fragile pause in the U.S.-Iran conflict has shattered after Iran fired ballistic missiles at a U.S. military base in Jordan in what CENTCOM described as an "attempted surprise attack." All missiles were intercepted with no U.S. casualties, but the attack prompted a fresh American retaliatory barrage lasting roughly two hours that struck "dozens" of Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps targets, including sites on Qeshm Island and near Bushehr. The U.S. and Saudi Arabia also conducted joint strikes on Iranian-backed militias in Iraq, and Jordan reported intercepting additional missiles targeting its territory.

The renewed fighting has raised fears of a return to all-out war after weeks of escalation since the conflict began February 28. Oil prices climbed back above $91 per barrel on the renewed hostilities, and stocks fell sharply with the Dow dropping more than 1,150 points. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu, meeting with President Trump at the White House, expressed skepticism about the prospects for a deal and discussed increasing economic pressure on Iran through "kinetic and non-kinetic means." Saudi Arabia, despite participating in the Iraq strikes, sent its defense minister to Washington to reiterate that Riyadh still favors de-escalation.

In a separate but related development, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile likely crossed into Polish territory overnight, leaving a 10-meter-wide crater in a field in eastern Poland near the Ukrainian border during a massive Russian assault on Lviv that killed at least eight people. Poland scrambled fighter jets and is conducting pyrotechnical analysis to confirm the missile's origin. No casualties were reported on Polish soil, but the incident triggered emergency consultations with European leaders and raised acute concerns about NATO airspace integrity.

A Russian missile landing on NATO territory — even without casualties — carries significant alliance implications and echoes a similar incident in November 2022. Ukraine's acting foreign minister confirmed the missile crossed into Poland as part of Russia's wider strike campaign. Polish officials said they were prepared to shoot it down had it continued its flight path.

stories.headline: Update: Federal Reserve Holds Rates for Fifth Straight Meeting in Divided Vote as Iran Conflict Fuels Inflation Pressure
stories.summary:
The Federal Reserve left its benchmark interest rate unchanged Wednesday in a 9-3 vote, marking the fifth consecutive meeting without a rate change. Three dissenting members — Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari, and a third official — voted in favor of a quarter-point rate increase, the first three-way dissent in over a decade. Fed officials indicated they expect inflation to ease, but the decision came under intense scrutiny given persistent inflation pressure exacerbated by rising energy prices tied to the U.S.-Iran conflict.

The hold disappointed markets: the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell more than 1,150 points, its worst single-day drop since the April 2025 "Liberation Day" tariff announcement, while the S&P 500 declined 1.52 percent. U.S. 30-year Treasury yields hit their highest level since 2007 following the decision. Brent crude oil traded near $91 per barrel, well off its recent highs above $101 but rising again as fighting between the U.S. and Iran resumed.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has made taming inflation a stated priority, but his reluctance to embrace higher borrowing costs has drawn criticism from within the central bank and on Wall Street. The three dissenting votes signal growing internal pressure to act more aggressively. Some analysts noted that China's withdrawal from global oil markets as a buyer has helped contain the worst potential price spikes from the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: Update: Rushdie Attacker Convicted of Terrorism Charges, Now Faces Possible Life Sentence
stories.summary:
Hadi Matar, already serving a 25-year state prison sentence for the 2022 stabbing of author Salman Rushdie, was convicted Wednesday in a New York federal court on additional charges of engaging in transnational terrorism and providing material support to Hezbollah. Prosecutors argued Matar was motivated by a 2006 speech by then-Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah calling for enforcement of the 1989 fatwa issued by Iran's supreme leader calling for Rushdie's death, and that he had plotted the attack for two years.

Rushdie himself testified at the Buffalo, New York trial, describing being stabbed 15 times on stage and lifting the darkened lens of his glasses to reveal his injured eye, which left him partially blind. "I was on the stage, lying down, with an enormous pool of blood all around me," Rushdie testified, adding the knife came "within millimetres from my brain." A firefighter's immediate medical response, Rushdie said, saved his life.

Defense attorneys argued the attack was not terrorism-motivated and questioned Rushdie about anticipated backlash to his 1988 novel "The Satanic Verses." Rushdie rejected the framing: "I don't believe the book is on trial. Somebody else is on trial." Matar now faces a potential life sentence when sentenced on the federal conviction, on top of his existing state term.

stories.headline: Ugandan Opposition Leader Kizza Besigye Collapses in Court, Hospitalized Unconscious in ICU
stories.summary:
Veteran Ugandan opposition leader Kizza Besigye, 70, collapsed and lost consciousness in a Kampala courtroom Wednesday while objecting to state-appointed lawyers being assigned to represent him in his treason trial. His wife, Winnie Byanyima — who heads UNAIDS — said he was admitted to the ICU at Mulago National Referral Hospital, describing him as "unconscious, unable to speak, and unresponsive even to a pain stimulus."

Besigye has been held in detention since November 2024 after being abducted from Kenya and returned to Uganda, where he and an aide face treason charges they deny, alleging they plotted to overthrow President Yoweri Museveni. Treason is a capital offense in Uganda. His primary lawyer was jailed last month on related charges, and a Kenyan attorney brought in to represent him was barred from entering the country.

Family members and human rights groups have called for Besigye's release on medical grounds, with his son writing an open letter to President Museveni and the army chief appealing for humanitarian consideration. Besigye refused treatment from government medical personnel but his sister, who is also a doctor, was eventually allowed access to him. The ICU ward is guarded by heavily armed security officers.
